title: Tagliatelle al Ragù Bolognese
subtitle: The proper slow-cooked Bolognese
excerpt: The Bolognese registered with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce: beef and pork mince, soffritto, tomato paste, white wine, whole milk, and a three-hour simmer. Served with egg tagliatelle, never spaghetti.

recipe.sourceNotes: The authentic recipe for ragù alla bolognese was registered with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce in 1982 by the Bolognese delegation of the Italian Academy of Cuisine. It specifies beef and pork mince, soffritto, tomato paste, dry white wine, and whole milk added gradually during the cook. Tagliatelle is the only acceptable pasta.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, heavy pot for the long simmer.

content.text: The proper Bolognese has very little tomato, a couple of tablespoons of paste, not tinned tomatoes. It is a meat sauce, and the meat is what the sauce is about. The milk goes in during cooking and softens the acidity of the wine. The three-hour simmer at the lowest possible heat is not optional, it is when the collagen from the meat breaks down and the sauce becomes glossy and deeply savoury.
Melt the butter in a wide, heavy pot over medium heat. Add the pancetta and cook for 3 minutes. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook gently for 12 minutes until very soft and sweet.
Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the beef and pork mince and cook, breaking it up, for 8 minutes until browned and any liquid has evaporated completely.
Pour in the white wine and stir. Cook until the wine has completely evaporated, about 5 minutes.
Add the milk in a thin stream, stirring. Cook until the milk has absorbed, about 5 minutes. Add the tomato puree and stock. Season with salt and pepper.

Reduce the heat to the lowest setting, half-cover with a lid, and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, stirring every 30 minutes and adding a splash of water or stock if the sauce reduces too far. The finished ragù should be dense, not saucy.
Cook the tagliatelle in well-salted boiling water. Drain, reserving pasta water. Toss with the ragù, adding a splash of pasta water to bring everything together. Serve with grated parmesan.
